data.title: Hours-long Microsoft outage disrupts businesses, governments globally
data.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - A more than 12-hour outage of Microsoft Outlook and Teams crippled communications for businesses and governments globally on Friday, forcing some organizations to revert to fax machines and halting at least one bond repurchase in Europe.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) said server issues were behind the incident that also affected its Copilot AI assistant and that a broader roll-out of software fixes was starting to stabilize the system. It said it was not aware of any malicious activity.

Outlook and Teams are two of the most widely used workplace applications with hundreds of millions of users. The outage prevented people from performing essential functions such as sending emails, managing calendars and hosting virtual meetings.

It affected government agencies from Australia to Japan and the United States, caused delays at trading firms, hindered some companies from publishing earnings and prompted airlines to warn customers of communication lags, according to public statements.

Organizations that host Microsoft ( MSFT ) services on their own servers, rather than in the cloud, were somewhat spared.

ANOTHER OUTAGE FOR MICROSOFT

The outage is one of the longest in Microsoft's ( MSFT ) history and the second disruption to its services this year.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) said the outage specifically hit features tied to Exchange Online - its cloud-based email and scheduling hub - leaving unconnected applications operational.

The incident deepens questions about the global reliance on a handful of Big Tech companies that supply both the essential software and the cloud infrastructure that underpins it.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) shares were down 0.4% in early trading. They have gained roughly 8% so far this year.

Disruptions and financial losses from the outage could result in numerous insurance claims, but the overall hit to insurers is expected to be limited, said Mario De Cicco, vice president of European financial institutions at Morningstar DBRS.

De Cicco estimated global insured losses from the incident at between $300 million and $500 million, well below the $400 million to $1.5 billion financial toll from the 2024 CrowdStrike outage that crashed more than 8 million Windows-based computers and caused widespread disruptions.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) also faced an outage with its 365 services in January this year and in October last year. Last month, it reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that impacted its suite of productivity software, and a range of industries worldwide. 

"The bigger worry is that this is not the first Microsoft ( MSFT ) 365 outage this year," said Josh Gilbert, a market analyst at trading platform eToro.

"If reliability starts to look like a recurring problem, it hands every IT department a reason to think twice before putting even more of their business in one provider's hands."

Still, some analysts have questioned whether such incidents can push customers on to rivals due to the steep switching costs of replacing tools embedded so deeply in daily operations.

TRADES HAD TO BE CONFIRMED BY FAX

A spokesperson for the UK government said it was working with Microsoft ( MSFT ) to find a solution for the outage that hit organizations such as the NHS and London's Metropolitan Police.

Lack of access emails and other services was impacting the Metropolitan Police's ability to report some crimes online, though its ability to respond to calls was not affected.

NHS said its local services were turning to alternate measures such as using IT systems or paper records.

For businesses, the fallout was widespread.

European exchange operator Euronext reported email disruptions, British insurer Aviva activated backups for its earnings calls and Danish shipping giant Maersk warned customers of delayed updates.

American AI giants OpenAI and Anthropic also faced issues with Microsoft ( MSFT ) connectors, while Indian airlines IndiGo, Akasa Air and Air India said their email support services were impacted.

The outage also disrupted fund management at Taiwanese securities firms, life insurers, and investment trust companies. One of the companies went as far as cancelling a bond repurchase transaction, a source familiar with the situation told Reuters.

Another Taiwanese financial company resorted to using fax to confirm trades, a second source said.

In the US, electric truck maker Workhorse Group rescheduled its results on Thursday to November 16, while Switzerland's Richemont briefly delayed its first-half results announcement on Friday.  

In Australia, where the spy agency and federal police were among organizations caught in the outage, Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke said Microsoft ( MSFT ) does not suspect a cyber attack.

"The impact that they are dealing with ... is very much on email systems," the minister added.

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- YouArt, an AI-powered creative platform backed by Y Combinator, announces the launch of YouArt Desktop App, a new AI video agent for Mac and PC that works directly with local project files, professional creative applications, and team feedback. Unlike AI video generators that focus on producing individual clips, YouArt Desktop App can understand existing projects, operate editing software, and carry out production tasks from initial research to final export.

From Client Feedback to Finished Revision

Image: YouArt Desktop App interface

When a client sends feedback through Slack or Gmail, YouArt Desktop App can bring it directly into the project canvas as a comment pinned to the relevant shot, frame, or creative element. The agent then uses that feedback to make the requested changes, while the creator reviews the revisions and decides what to keep.

The canvas stores project materials, including footage, scripts, brand assets, and generated clips, along with comments and version history. This gives creators and the agent a shared view of the project, keeping feedback, assets, and revisions connected throughout production.

An AI Agent That Works Inside Professional Editing Software

Image: YouArt exporting editable motion graphics titles directly into Adobe After Effects

Beyond organizing project materials and feedback, YouArt Desktop App can carry out production tasks directly in professional creative applications. With the user's permission, the agent can operate Adobe After Effects, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, CapCut, and Blender by navigating menus, clicking, and entering commands. Creators can continue using their existing projects, templates, and plugins without switching to a new editing environment.

For example, when creating a product launch video, a marketing team can use YouArt Desktop App to turn existing product assets and brand materials into a storyboard, visuals, and motion graphics. The agent can generate animations directly within YouArt Desktop App and export them to After Effects for further refinement, while the team reviews the work and makes final adjustments.

Reusable agent skills also support specialized tasks such as story development, shot planning, commercial video production, and motion design, helping creators apply established workflows to new projects.

YouArt Desktop App also supports Chat to Edit, allowing creators to refine videos through natural-language instructions. A user can select an element and request changes such as "use our brand blue" or "hold this title for one more second." The agent applies targeted revisions while preserving the rest of the project, and manual timeline controls remain available for precise adjustments.

YouArt Desktop App also includes built-in browser tabs for researching ideas, gathering references, and using web-based tools. Users can see when the agent is operating a page and take control at any time.

Smart Routing: Always the Lowest Price for the Selected Model

Image: YouArt Launches YouArt Desktop App, AI Creative Teammate on the Computer

Traditional AI creative platforms often bundle model access into their own pricing, making it difficult for creators to see individual model costs or compare prices across providers. YouArt Desktop App takes a different approach by allowing creators to bring their own API keys and connect to third-party providers, including Higgsfield, fal, and BytePlus. Its smart routing system compares provider prices and automatically selects the lowest-priced option for the chosen model.

Alongside its built-in models, YouArt Desktop App supports video and image generation, voiceovers, music, lip sync, and avatars within the same workflow, including ElevenLabs v3 for voiceovers and Suno for original music.

YouArt Desktop App offers Seedance 2.5 video generation at 720p for $0.208 per second on a pay-as-you-go basis, approximately 56% less than fal and 55% less than Higgsfield, based on the company's pricing comparison. The rate drops to $0.138 per second with the YouArt Max yearly plan, offering savings of up to 71% compared with fal.

A Creative Team for Social Content, Feature Launches and Film Projects

Image: YouArt Desktop App

For social media marketers, YouArt Desktop App can research trending videos, analyze their hooks, pacing, and structure, and help create original content using a brand's own assets. Its AutoClip workflow can also turn long-form footage into short clips with captions and platform-specific formatting, ready for publishing or scheduling.

For feature launches, marketing teams can use YouArt Desktop App to turn product documentation, pitch decks, and brand assets into storyboards, product demonstrations, and promotional videos. The agent helps develop visuals and motion graphics, while creators review the work and refine the final video.

For film projects, YouArt Desktop App supports script development, storyboarding, consistent characters, scene generation, and collaborative editing. By assisting across production stages, the agent can take on tasks typically handled by a creative team, helping filmmakers bring ideas from concept to completion.

To learn more about YouArt Desktop App, visit https://youart.ai.

Backed by Y Combinator, the company combines advanced AI models and creative tools to support storytelling, video production, and commercial content creation. With a mission to democratize creativity, YouArt aims to make professional video production more accessible, efficient, and scalable.

data.title: Egan-Jones Examines How Falling Development Costs Could Reshape Video Games
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Egan-Jones released a commentary examining why Grand Theft Auto VI, due November 19, may mark the end of an era of expensive video game development. The piece finds that artificial intelligence has cut the capital needed to develop and port games, and offers investors a framework for the shift.

Video games are a business of about $200 billion a year, six times the box office, and 85% of US teens play them, according to the commentary. Outside estimates put development of Grand Theft Auto VI at $1.0 billion to $1.5 billion, or $1.5 billion to $2.0 billion including marketing. Its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, earned about 30 times what it cost.

Egan-Jones believes owners of well-recognized intellectual property hold a major advantage, because familiar franchises can make marketing investment more successful. With development costs falling, these owners can open their franchises to anyone, license them broadly for a fee or royalty, or develop them in-house or with accountable partners. Egan-Jones expects owners most sensitive to tainting, such as Disney, to favor self-development or close partnerships.

For credit investors, the commentary describes a significant shift. Rather than funding a few large projects and studios, lenders may begin financing many smaller ones, which offers diversification but calls for more due diligence. Egan-Jones also expects growing demand to finance marketing, which it describes as generally safer than financing development because creditors sidestep the risk of "development hell."

The commentary also points to pressure on established players. Developers such as BioWare and Ubisoft have closed or significantly reduced operations, and Egan-Jones writes that Microsoft's studio acquisitions may have been poor investments given the shift in costs. It adds that platforms controlling product discovery should continue to benefit: players spent about $82 billion on mobile games through the App Store and Google Play in 2025, and Steam reached a record 43.5 million concurrent users on October 11.

Egan-Jones concludes that Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to be one of the largest launches in entertainment history and may still be the last of its kind. For lenders, the new model needs less financing over the long term.

data.title: European shares end best week since June as strong earnings lift sentiment
data.description:
(Updates after markets close)

* AI outlook concerns after Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Huang's resignation weigh on tech

* UK's Wise Group tops STOXX index after H1 results

* Richemont drops after disappointing Q2 jewellery sales

* Goldman Sachs raises 12-month target for STOXX 600

* Euro zone third-quarter GDP grows 0.4% quarter-on-quarter

By Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair, Johann M Cherian and Avinash P

Nov 13 (Reuters) - European shares were little changed on Friday, but recorded their best week since late June as strong earnings and a rotation out of tech globally helped investors look past geopolitical risks and the volatility involving AI stocks.

The STOXX 600 closed flat at 664.14 points, and gained over 2% for the week. Heavyweight Euro STOXX banks index rose over 4% this week and led broader gains.

Robust earnings, along with a fall in oil prices on hopes of a potential easing of the US-Iran conflict earlier this week, helped the STOXX 600 breach record-high levels for the first time since August on Thursday.

Analysts also pointed to structural tailwinds that could boost Europe's prospects in the long term.

"Europe is building its rearmament program, its industrial program, strategic autonomy, its energy infrastructure and its defence," said Jitania Kandhari, deputy CIO, Solutions & Multi-Assets at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

"That is trickling into different pockets of the economy and the markets now. When investment in capex picks up, it has spillover effects," she said.

Mirroring the optimism, Goldman Sachs raised its 12-month target for the STOXX 600 to 700 points from 695.

TECH LOSES STEAM

On Friday, the tech sector fell 1.3%, leading losses.

Uncertainty over the outlook for the AI trade rippled through global markets following Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation as Nvidia's ( NVDA ) CEO, as investors fretted about the future of the AI goliath that has underpinned much of the rally in global markets.

Chip stocks such as Infineon and Aixtron were down more than 4% each, while AI equipment makers such as Schneider Electric and Legrand were also lower.

Adding to caution, crude prices swung in the session as Washington's focus on blockading Iran and ramping up other economic pressures allayed fears of renewed direct conflict in the Middle East.

Investors also weighed some corporate earnings on Friday.

Wise Group gained 7.7% to top the benchmark index after the money transfer company reported a 23% net revenue rise in the first half of its fiscal year.

In contrast, Richemont fell 3.8% after the Cartier owner reported weaker-than-expected sales in its jewellery unit during the second quarter.

Acciona fell 8%, languishing at the bottom of the index after subsidiary Acciona Energia said it would not meet its €2 billion ($2.21 billion) target for its asset rotation programme.

On the data front, the euro zone economy grew by 0.4% quarter-on-quarter in the third quarter, according to a flash gross domestic product estimate from the EU's statistics agency.

($1 = 0.9065 euros)

(Reporting by Anjana J Nair, Johann M Cherian and Avinash P in Bengaluru; Editing by Mrigank Dhaniwala, Jochelle Mendonca and Xevi Fontdegloria)

* Oil majors BP and Shell gained about 1.5% each as crude prices edged higher following strikes on Saudi Arabian infrastructure by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and attacks on tankers shipping crude out of the Gulf

data.title: H&R REIT unitholders reject breakup deal after failed vote
data.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - Canada's H&R Real Estate Investment Trust said on Friday its unitholders voted against a previously announced C$6.7 billion ($4.7 billion) breakup deal.

The deal, announced in August, was meant to close a multi-year effort to simplify H&R's portfolio and sharpen its focus on residential real estate.

* H&R had agreed to the breakup deal, under which GO Residential REIT was to acquire its residential portfolio in the US, while a group including Blackstone and entities tied to H&R CEO Tom Hofstedter would buy the other assets

* Unitholders rejected the deal at a special meeting on Friday, prompting H&R to terminate the arrangement with immediate effect

* No termination fee would be payable to the consortium, it said

* H&R will also back away from a proposed purchase of a 70% interest in two joint venture development properties owned by Lantower Residential Real Estate Development Trust that it announced in October

* The company plans to reinstate monthly distributions, pursue asset sales and begin a board rejig that would include CEO succession planning

data.title: Anthropic sued for trademark infringement over 'Mythos' model

* Mythos, which operates a software platform for nonprofit organizations, told the court that Anthropic's Mythos AI model will create market confusion and cause it "great and irreparable injury"

* Mythos asked the court for an unspecified amount of monetary damages and a court order blocking Anthropic from using the "Mythos" name

* Spokespeople for Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the complaint

Nov 13 (Reuters) - Shares of AI-related US companies dropped again on Friday, with neoclouds among the worst hit, fueled by fresh jitters over AI financing following Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt exit.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 declined 2%, on pace to erase about $800 billion in market value if the losses hold through the close. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index also shed 5.1%, facing a more than $560 billion wipeout for the day.

CoreWeave and Nebius Group, neocloud firms backed by Nvidia ( NVDA ), slumped 8.8% and 9%, respectively, extending their sharp declines from Thursday when longtime CEO Huang stepped down after revelations of extramarital affairs.

Nvidia ( NVDA ), under Huang, has financed infrastructure built around its chips, a strategy that has driven demand but also raised questions about circular funding flows between the chipmaker and its customers.

"It's a short-term death blow to the industry because the amount of vendor financing and financing guarantees that Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Jensen Huang stepped into are now over," said Thomas Hayes, chairman of Great Hill Capital LLC.

Further, Nscale, a British cloud provider also backed by Nvidia ( NVDA ), amended its IPO filing to say it expects to report a net loss of $1.7 billion in the nine months ended September 30, wider than the $433.3 million net loss a year ago.

A media report on Friday said Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Huang. Arm shares were last down 4.8%.

Chip stocks, widely regarded as among the biggest winners of the AI boom, also dropped. Advanced Micro Devices fell 10.7% and Broadcom lost 5.9% after both gained for the last five sessions.

Memory chipmaker Micron Technology shed 5% while data storage companies Western Digital and Sandisk dipped 6.6% and 8.1%, respectively.

Photonic product makers Lumentum and Coherent, along with AI server makers Dell and HPE, fell between 5.3% and 9% each.

Utilities and equipment suppliers exposed to the AI boom, including GE Vernova, Constellation Energy and Vistra, eased about 2.2% to 3.5% each.

AI hyperscalers were also mostly lower, barring Meta Platforms, which rose 1.2%. Oracle, Alphabet, Amazon.com and Microsoft fell between 0.2% and 2.7%.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) quarterly earnings and AI lab Anthropic's much-awaited public markets debut are set for next week and could prove to be catalysts for sentiment towards AI.

"You have no idea what to expect from Nvidia ( NVDA ). That's the problem. This company is pure uncertainty right now," said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers.

(Reporting by Shashwat Chauhan in Bengaluru; Additional reporting by Darshan Kumar and Anjana J. Nair; Editing by Joyjeet Das)

data.title: Atom Computing Finalizes $100 Million U.S. Department of Commerce R&D Award to Accelerate Fault-Tolerant, Utility-Scale Quantum Computing
data.description:
Funding will advance the commercialization of logical-qubit quantum computers and strengthen U.S. leadership in quantum technology.

BOULDER, Colo.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Atom Computing, a leader in scalable neutral-atom quantum computing, today announced it has signed an agreement for up to $100 million with the U.S. Department of Commerce to accelerate research and development of fault-tolerant, utility-scale quantum computers. The award follows a Letter of Intent announced earlier this year and represents a significant investment in advancing next-generation computing technologies critical to U.S. economic competitiveness, scientific leadership, and national security.

Atom Computing's neutral-atom architecture is increasingly recognized as one of the most viable approaches for building large-scale, commercially useful quantum computers. Today’s announcement closely follows the company’s recent selection as the only neutral atom company to advance to Stage C of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (DARPA QBI) with potential funding up to $300 million.

Atom has consistently demonstrated technical leadership through several industry milestones, including being the first to build a platform with more than 1,000 qubits, the first neutral-atom company to demonstrate sub-threshold behavior on a system with full, end-to-end quantum error correction over many rounds, and the first to commercially offer a logical-qubit quantum computer. In 2025 Atom Computing sold its first commercial on-premises quantum computer to QuNorth, a Nordic quantum initiative funded by EIFO and Novo Nordisk Foundation.

"Quantum computing is reaching a critical inflection point where scientific breakthroughs must rapidly translate into commercial reality," said Dr. Ben Bloom, CEO and Founder of Atom Computing. "This $100 million contract enables us to aggressively scale the engineering required to bring fault-tolerant quantum computing to market and ensure the United States leads the transition into the utility-scale era."

The Department of Commerce contract will accelerate several of Atom Computing’s strategic R&D initiatives which will shorten the timeline to economically viable quantum computing, including:

  • Developing critical technologies in-house to improve system performance, reliability, and vertical integration
  • Expanding parallel engineering and testbed infrastructure to rapidly validate innovations and speed product development
  • Strengthening R&D collaboration with key supply chain partners to support manufacturing scale-up and long-term growth

Industry and government interest in practical quantum computing continues to accelerate, with advances in error correction, system scale, and hardware performance driving increased confidence in the technology's commercial potential. Atom Computing has demonstrated leadership in logical-qubit systems and fault-tolerant architectures, translating scientific breakthroughs into deployable commercial systems for real-world applications.

About Atom Computing

Atom Computing is developing large-scale quantum computers to enable companies and researchers to achieve unprecedented computational breakthroughs. Utilizing highly scalable arrays of optically trapped neutral atoms, the company has developed systems with over 1,000 qubits, featuring advanced capabilities towards fault-tolerant quantum computing. Atom Computing’s on-premises systems provide customers with new computational tools and logical qubit capabilities to address increasingly complex applications and to grow their quantum ecosystem. Learn more at atom-computing.com and follow us on LinkedIn.

data.title: European Stocks Close Mixed in Friday Trading; EU, Euro Area GDP Growth in Line With Projections
data.description:
11:51 AM EST, 11/13/2026 (MT Newswires) -- European stock markets closed mixed in Friday trading as the European Union and Euro area reported monthly and annual GDP growth that was in line with analyst forecasts.

The Stoxx Europe was off 0.1%, Germany's DAX declined 0.1%, the FTSE 100 rose 0.4%, France's CAC gained 0.1%, and the Swiss Market Index fell 0.3%.

Seasonally adjusted GDP increased by 0.4% in the euro area and by 0.5% in the EU in Q3, compared with the previous quarter, according to a flash estimate published by Eurostat, the statistical office of the EU. Compared with a year earlier, seasonally adjusted GDP increased by 1.3% in the euro area and 1.5% in the EU.

Both readings met expectations by analysts polled by Bloomberg.

Eurostat also reported that the number of employed remained unchanged in both the euro area and the EU in Q3, compared with the previous quarter. Compared with a year earlier, employment increased 0.4% in both the euro area and the EU.

In corporate news, Novo Nordisk said Friday it submitted etavopivat, a once-daily oral treatment for sickle cell disease in patients 12 and older, for approval with the US Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency.

A phase 3 trial showed the drug cut vaso-occlusive crises by 27% and delayed the first crisis by about four months versus placebo, the company said.

The FDA and European regulators are expected to decide on the applications in 2027, and etavopivat holds orphan and fast track designations, Novo Nordisk said.

Shares of the Danish pharmaceutical company rose 1% in Copenhagen.

AstraZeneca's Baxfendy, developed for the treatment of adults with insufficiently controlled hypertension, has been recommended for marketing authorization by the European Medicines Agency's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use, the agency said Friday.

The health agency said the recommendation is based on clinical trials showing statistically significant reductions in systolic and diastolic blood pressure compared with placebo in patients whose hypertension remained uncontrolled despite treatment with at least two medications.

The European Commission will make the final decision on marketing authorization, the agency said.

Shares of AstraZeneca increased 0.6% in London.

A French judge has ordered Hermes heir Nicolas Puech to undergo a cognitive assessment, Reuters reported Friday, citing two people with direct knowledge of the decision. Puech is suing the company, alleging he was cheated out of his 6% stake in the luxury goods giant.

Hermes didn't immediately respond to a request for comment from MT Newswires.

Shares of Hermes were 0.1% lower in Paris.

Nokia said Friday its Federal Solutions unit won a US Department of Defense contract to build systems using 5G and 6G networks to detect and track objects for threat awareness.

The project, known as Real-World Application Prototyping for ISAC Demonstration, combines multiple sensing methods on Nokia's AI-RAN platform to identify unmanned aircraft threats, the company said.

Texas Tech University, DeepSig, Hidden Level and Future Technologies are among subcontractors supporting the project, Nokia said.

Shares of Nokia rose 1% in Olso.

Novartis' Cosentyx was recommended for expanded use to treat adolescents aged 12 and older with moderate-to-severe hidradenitis suppurativa, a chronic skin condition that causes painful lumps and inflammation, the European Medicines Agency said Friday.

The recommendation covers adolescents who have not responded adequately to standard systemic treatments for the condition, the agency said.

The European Commission will make the final decision on the proposed change to the drug's marketing authorization, it added.

Shares of the Swiss pharmaceutical company edged 0.1% higher in Zurich.

GSK's Bexsero received a recommendation from the European Medicines Agency to immunize newborns against meningococcal disease, the regulator said Friday.

The EMA's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended the vaccine for meningococcal disease caused by Neisseria meningitidis group B in children from 6 weeks of age and older, compared with two months and older previously, the regulator said.

Shares of GSK gained 0.7% in London.

Alphen aan den Rijn, NL – November 13, 2026 – Wolters Kluwer Health has signed an agreement to acquire AgileMD, a healthcare technology company, for up to $100 million, of which $40 million is an upfront payment and the balance is a deferred consideration contingent upon reaching certain performance targets.

AgileMD provides AI-powered clinical decision support for health care professionals, offering them interactive clinical pathways and predictive analytics to enhance consistency in care and help them to reduce mortality rates. The company’s Pathways product operationalizes local guidelines in the EHR workflow for consistency in care and outcomes measurement. Its eCART solution is a real-time AI-powered clinical surveillance engine that is FDA1-cleared and designed to help reduce mortality rates.

“Combined with UpToDate Expert AI and our partnerships, AgileMD will serve as a vital enabler for true UpToDate ubiquity in healthcare – facilitating UpToDate’s expansion into embedded workflows, local guidelines, and new digital health applications,” said Yaw Fellin, Senior Vice President, Wolters Kluwer Clinical Solutions. “With AgileMD, we are well positioned to help healthcare systems provide better patient care and extract more value from their tech investments.”

Borna Safabakhsh, Co-Founder and CEO at AgileMD, commented, “We are excited to join Wolters Kluwer Health. Coupled with UpToDate, AgileMD can more fully deliver its transformative impact in critical decision support workflows. Leveraging UpToDate’s foundational capabilities, AgileMD will accelerate and streamline the development and maintenance of more advanced clinical pathways for complex clinical decision-making support.”

Since its introduction in September 2025, UpToDate Expert AI has been adopted by more than 2,700 U.S. hospitals and health systems, representing more than 95% of U.S.-based UpToDate Enterprise Edition customers.

Additional information and financial terms

AgileMD, based in San Francisco, was founded in 2011 and is currently led by co-founders Borna Safabakhsh and Dana Edelson, M.D., Chief Medical Officer. All 23 employees will be joining Wolters Kluwer Health. AgileMD has seen strong growth and is expected to reach annual recurring revenues (ARR) of $7 million by year-end 2026. The acquisition is expected to achieve a return on invested capital (ROIC) at or above our after-tax weighted average cost of capital (WACC) of 8% within 3-5 years and to have an immaterial impact on Wolters Kluwer adjusted earnings. The transaction, which is subject to customary closing conditions and other governmental approvals, is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027 or sooner.

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. data.title: Bessent, Fed's Goolsbee divided on role of energy shock in inflation
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday that the Federal Reserve should not hike rates because of inflation driven by an "energy supply shock" tied to the Iran war, comments made to CNBC and promptly contradicted on the network by Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, who said price pressures were building far beyond what could be explained by high oil prices.

"I think the Fed should understand that this is an energy supply shock," while the underlying US economy is very strong, Bessent said in an interview on CNBC. "So I think that to hike too much into an energy supply shock when it's coming down, these are very noisy numbers...You know, the Fed's supposed to look into the future, not look in the rearview mirror."

Shortly afterwards, the network hosted Goolsbee, a regular guest on CNBC's morning Squawk Box show, who said that inflation was not just due to energy, but had spread to the service sector and areas like medical care that are not usually responsive to the price of oil, and was also elevated through strong demand tied to the AI data center buildout.

"I respect the secretary and I am trying to figure out the same thing he is trying to figure out, which is how persistent is this inflation? The tariff inflation and oil price shock were supposed to have gone away by now and it hasn't," Goolsbee said. "One puzzle is why have those supply shocks been as persistent as they have been. A second thing is if demand is overheating and that is contributing to inflation, that is more worrisome... Services inflation, which is probably not coming from tariffs or oil, is one of the more troubling aspects of the inflation reports we have been getting."

While not committing to a rate hike, he said the Fed "has definitely got work to do to continue to reestablish its credibility."

The two interviews highlighted competing narratives about aspects of the US economy that figured heavily in midterm elections that centered on high inflation as well as the rapid pace of an AI buildout. The Trump administration has cheered the AI boom and focused on the likely upside, while being critical of communities reluctant to host the massive data centers needed for the technology.

Like other administration officials, Bessent focused on what he sees as the oil-driven roots of current inflation and criticized the Fed for responding to it.

"I'm not going to tell the Fed what to do. I am going to say they should have an open mind," Bessent said, noting that the Fed had cut rates last year, "and now to reverse just based on an energy supply shock, a reversal in a dramatic way isn't something that I would do if I were on the Fed. But I'm not on the Fed."

Fed policymakers were open to the possibility they could "look through" supply-driven inflation at the start of the US war with Iran. But as inflation remained lodged above the Fed's target, concern about it grew, as did support for rate hikes. Research meanwhile opened a different window on the relationship between oil prices and US inflation. Because the US is an energy exporter, higher global oil prices can filter through to the economy in the form of higher corporate profits and wages, providing a source of inflation beyond supply issues that can't be easily ignored by the central bank.

Recent stronger-than-expected jobs and inflation reports have further bolstered the case for more Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, and even prompted some officials to discuss the need for a larger-than-typical half-percentage-point increase at the central bank's coming December 8-9 meeting.

"We have had signs of trouble now for several months in a row if you look at how broad-based the inflation is," Goolsbee said. "In categories that are not driven by oil prices and not driven by tariffs, you are still seeing stalled progress and in some cases going the wrong way ... That is not going away no matter what happens to the price of oil."

"Are we on a path back to 2%? My feeling right now is we are not and we've got to deal with that," Goolsbee said. "Conventional wisdom says do everything you can to prevent demand overheating," Goolsbee said, with coming data on inflation the key to whether the Fed needs a faster pace of rate increases.

(Reporting by Doina Chiacu, Katharine Jackson and Howard Schneider; Editing by Alex Richardson, Doina Chiacu and Andrea Ricci )

data.title: Betterness Expands Seed Round to $3.5 Million to Build Neighborhood Health Networks in Miami
data.description:
The first network launches at Miami Worldcenter on Nov. 15 with more than 30 local businesses, a free member app and the software those businesses run on.

MIAMI, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Betterness, Inc., which builds neighborhood health networks that connect people with the gyms, studios, clinics, coaches, local brands and health services around them, today announced $1 million in additional seed financing, bringing its seed round to $3.5 million. A private investment group with deep pharmaceutical expertise led the extension. The other investors bring venture capital experience and have built companies in artificial intelligence, healthcare and blockchain.

People train, eat and recover with the businesses in their neighborhood. Their health data sits in separate apps, and those businesses run on separate tools. Most health technology stops at the app or the wearable. Betterness connects the member, the local business and the health services in one network, and Bett-i, the AI inside Betterness, works across all three.

Since its $2.5 million seed round and the launch of Bett-i in April, Betterness has moved its business customers from beta to daily operations. Locations process an average of $500,000 a year in member bookings through Betterness One. Betterness will use the new financing to grow the network one neighborhood at a time, starting with Miami Worldcenter and then Miami Beach.

"The front line of health and wellness is the small business that opens its doors every day," said Demian Bellumio, Co-Founder and Co-CEO of Betterness. "We ran Betterness in beta with exceptional Miami businesses that trusted us to go deep inside their operations and rethink how they run from the ground up. What we built with them runs their businesses today, and now we are accelerating deployment. Betterness connects everyone who helps a person live better, in the real world, not inside an app. Miami is the best city to launch it, and Miami Worldcenter is where it starts."

How the network works

For members, Betterness is a free app. Members track more than 70 sports in the app or on Apple Watch, sync Garmin, Oura and Withings devices, log meals from a photo and order lab tests across the U.S. through Quest Diagnostics and BioReference. Bett-i turns that data into guidance and builds training programs from hundreds of video tutorials for strength, Pilates and yoga. When Betterness introduced Bett-i in April, Men's Fitness asked whether it was "the most ambitious AI health product ever built."

For businesses, Betterness One puts the tools a wellness business uses today in one place. In Grow, free for every business, owners publish a Space in the Betterness app, offer perks, follow their Instagram and post with Bett-i. In Host, staff sell memberships and class packs, take payments, run schedules, bookings and check-in, and put a live heart-rate board on the screen in the room. In Coach, now in beta, coaches keep a training file for every member, and Bett-i adjusts each program for the coach to approve. With Sell, coming soon, businesses will sell products inside the app.

Members decide what each business and coach sees. Bett-i runs on the Betterness Graph, where Betterness connects each member's data, with the member's permission, to the businesses and coaches they choose. Businesses and members choose the GPT or Claude model that fits them, or connect their own AI tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Betterness is a HIPAA-compliant platform with strict data controls. Any health and wellness business can start free with Grow at betterness.one.

"A studio or clinic can run its entire operation on Betterness One," said Ari Katz, Co-Founder and Co-CEO of Betterness. "Its members decide what to share, under strict data controls, and the business uses that to personalize classes, programs and offers in a way traditional wellness business software never could."

Why Miami Worldcenter first

At full build-out, Miami Worldcenter is planned for up to 40,000 residents in and around it. Its weekly Night Market draws more than 60 vendors. Many are small wellness businesses. Betterness built the Worldcenter Perks program with more than 30 businesses in the district and nearby. Wynwood Padel Club offers members 20% off court bookings. SWEAT440 takes part through its Brickell and Midtown studios.

Betterness launches the network at the Miami Worldcenter Wellness Series: Feeling ALIVE on Sunday, Nov. 15, from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. More than 600 people have registered. Readers can download the free Betterness app for iPhone or Android and join the Miami Worldcenter Space today. What Betterness builds at Worldcenter becomes the model for its next neighborhoods and for other cities in the U.S. and abroad.

What comes next

Betterness will add telemedicine with licensed clinicians, prescriptions filled by licensed U.S. pharmacies when a clinician prescribes them, and a curated supplement line. Members will reach these services through the local businesses they use, and those businesses need no clinical network or pharmacy of their own.

Better Health. Better Life. Together.

About Betterness

Betterness is a Miami-based health technology company building neighborhood health and wellness networks. Betterness brings a member's workouts, sleep, nutrition and lab results into one free app, with Bett-i, the AI inside Betterness. With Betterness One, gyms, studios, clinics, coaches and local brands grow, host and coach, with selling coming soon. Learn more at betterness.ai and betterness.one. Betterness provides wellness information, not medical advice.

About Miami Worldcenter

Miami Worldcenter is a new $6 billion mixed-use destination in the heart of Downtown Miami. As one of the largest private urban real estate developments underway in the United States, the project occupies 27 acres spanning ten city blocks and offers world-class retail, hospitality, commercial and residential uses. Several phases of the project have already been completed and occupied, including three residential towers, a significant portion of the retail component, and a citizenM hotel.

Miami Worldcenter Associates serves as the master developer for the overall mixed-use development, led by Managing Partners Art Falcone and Nitin Motwani, in partnership with CIM Group, a community-focused real estate and infrastructure owner, operator, lender and developer. Together they have assembled a best-in-class development team that is currently transforming the urban core of Miami into one of the country's largest mixed-use destinations. Learn more at www.miamiworldcenter.com.

data.title: Wall St reverses early gains as Nvidia fallout rattles tech stocks
data.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - The major US stock indexes fell on Friday as fresh concerns about Nvidia ( NVDA ) reignited a selloff in technology shares, while softer October producer prices data offered little relief.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) shares plunged 4.3% and were on track for their longest streak of weekly losses since October 2012 after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday, following scrutiny of his relationship with a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for Beijing.

The turmoil has raised concerns about the AI trade, given Nvidia's ( NVDA ) central role in the industry's boom and its financial ties to several companies in the sector.

The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 6%, with Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom dropping 10% and 7%, respectively. 

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius shed 10% each, while data center-related firms IREN, Applied Digital and Core Scientific declined between 3% and 9%.

The losses leave equities vulnerable heading into Anthropic's much-anticipated IPO next week, which could test investor appetite for established AI heavyweights as money potentially shifts toward the new entrant.

"Something that will be interesting to see is if all the supply of new equity is going to be absorbed in a way that doesn't result in selling other AI stocks to kind of fund that," said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global investment strategist at Edward Jones.

At 11:23 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 122.12 points, or 0.23%, to 52,174.97, the S&P 500 lost 76.88 points, or 1.01%, to 7,515.49, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 441.78 points, or 1.74%, to 24,923.79.

Among the Magnificent Seven, Apple and Meta were the only gainers, rising less than 1% each. Microsoft was down 0.4% after a more than 12-hour outage of Outlook and Teams.

INFLATION CONCERNS REMAIN

The tech index was the biggest loser on the S&P 500, dropping 3%. Six of the 11 major S&P sector indexes were in negative territory.

In economic data, the October Producer Price Index for final demand was slightly softer than expected, but still shot up 6.5% year over year, its largest annual gain since November 2022.

"That's definitely not good, especially on the heels of a rotten CPI (Consumer Price Index) number earlier this week. It shows that inflation continues to be a problem," said Jon Zetlmaier, founder of Zetlmaier Wealth Management.

In other movers, Cerebras jumped more than 6% after the chip and cloud company raised its 2026 revenue forecast and signed Microsoft as a customer.

Strong earnings have at certain points kept negative market sentiment in check this week. Of the 450 companies in the S&P 500 that reported earnings as of Thursday, 83.6% surpassed expectations, according to Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings and equity research at LSEG Data and Analytics.

Investors, though, are wary of a bunch of risks, including on the geopolitical front. Oil prices were in positive territory for the third consecutive session, a day after President Donald Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.49-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 2.03-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 9 new 52-week highs and 1 new low, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 22 new highs and 258 new lows.

(Reporting by Niket Nishant and Utkarsh Hathi in Bengaluru; Editing by Shinjini Ganguli and Pooja Desai)

data.title: GlobalFoundries breaks ground on first new semiconductor fab under landmark U.S.-Japan initiative

MALTA, N.Y., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- GlobalFoundries ( GFS ) today joined U.S. and Japanese government officials, state and local leaders, customers, partners, employees and community members to break ground on the first new semiconductor manufacturing facility planned for its Malta, New York, site under a landmark U.S.-Japan initiative. The groundbreaking marks the start of construction on a new 300mm fab and a first-of-its-kind model that brings together Japanese investment with GF’s technology and manufacturing expertise to expand trusted U.S. semiconductor capacity and support growing demand across automotive, industrial and connected infrastructure markets.

The groundbreaking follows GF’s Oct. 14 announcement that it was selected as the technology provider and operator for two new fabs at its Malta site under a U.S.-Japan initiative providing up to $21 billion in funding. Japan will provide the investment, while GF will contribute its differentiated technologies, manufacturing expertise and proven operational capabilities. An initial investment of approximately $10 billion, supported with $570 million in incentives from New York State is accelerating construction of the first fab, which is expected to come online in 2029. An additional investment of approximately $10 billion will support a second fab as the project advances.

data.title: FOREX-Dollar set for biggest weekly gain in two months
data.description:
* Dollar holds firm as traders ramp up rate hike bets

* Fed officials caution on inflation

* Yen just shy of 160 per dollar, stirring intervention worries

* Aussie dollar feels the heat from rising US yields

(Updates headline and prices throughout, adds analyst comment)

By Chibuike Oguh and Javi West Larrañaga

NEW YORK/GDANSK, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The dollar was on track for its strongest weekly rise in two months on Friday, holding near a 19-month high as rising bets on a larger Federal Reserve rate hike lifted US Treasury yields, while the yen hovered around 160 per dollar and kept traders alert for possible intervention from Tokyo.

Hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials and this week's stronger-than-expected US inflation data have left traders weighing the prospect of a larger-than-usual Fed rate hike next month.

Two-year Treasury yields have risen around 32 basis points so far this week to around 4.84%, on course for their biggest weekly jump since April 2025.

The euro was down 0.23% at $1.103, after hitting its lowest level against the dollar since April 2025. It was on course for its fourth straight week of losses.

The dollar was up 0.28% to 0.837 against the Swiss franc and was set to snap two straight weeks of losses.

"The dollar is still firm and that's driven by a robust jobs report and an acceleration of the CPI," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex. "We've had a series of hawkish comments from Fed officials this week including from (New York Fed President John) Williams and (Fed Governor Christopher) Waller."

Traders are pricing in a roughly 92% chance of a 25-basis-point hike next month, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, was up 0.1% at 103.34, clinging to its highest since April 2025 and on track for its biggest weekly gain since September. That would be its third straight week of gains.

YEN FOCUS

The yen was steady at 159.84 per dollar, around its weakest since early September, fuelling concerns about possible intervention. The currency has weakened about 1% this week, on track for its biggest weekly loss since September.

Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday the government would respond appropriately to currency volatility.

The Australian dollar was down 0.46% at $0.678. The Aussie is the worst-performing G10 currency against the dollar so far this month. Australia is the only G10 country for which markets are pricing a rate cut next year.

The New Zealand kiwi weakened 0.29% versus the greenback to $0.553 and was on course for its third straight week of losses.

In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 4.73% to $68,126.21. Ethereum declined 5.02% to $1,914.61.

(Reporting by Chibuike Oguh in New York and Javi West Larrañaga in Gdansk. Editing by Susan Fenton)

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Modern Automotive Diagnostics has evolved far beyond plugging in a code reader and clearing fault flags. With contemporary vehicles integrating 60 to 100 electronic control units (ECUs) across powertrain, chassis, and body domains, technicians now run multi-brand diagnostic suites, interface with vehicle communication interface (VCI) and Pass-Thru hardware, read ECU topology and freeze-frame data, and perform online programming and flashing. These tasks demand computing power, interface breadth, and stability that consumer-grade devices simply cannot deliver—especially inside a repair bay.

Workshops and roadside assistance environments represent a hostile ecosystem for standard electronics: constant vibration, accidental drops, oil and dust contamination, extreme temperature swings, and the need to operate touchscreens with wet or gloved hands. More critically, consumer laptops or tablets lack native RS232 serial, Gigabit Ethernet, and direct OBD-II protocol support, forcing technicians to rely on a cascade of adapters that introduce connection failures at the worst possible moment. Emdoor Information (Stock Code: 001314.SZ), an A-share listed specialist in rugged smart terminals with nearly two decades of domain expertise, has developed a portfolio built around the rugged AI laptop and rugged AI tablet, engineered specifically to close the gap between diagnostic software, vehicle connectivity, and field operations.

Built for the Bay: Rugged by Design

In Automotive Diagnostics, a dropped connection during an ECU flash can render a control unit inoperable—a costly mistake measured in thousands of dollars and hours of recovery. Emdoor Info's rugged AI laptop and rugged AI tablet families are designed to eliminate that risk at the hardware level. Every unit carries IP65 ingress protection and MIL-STD-810H certification, ensuring resistance to dust, pressurized water jets, vibration, and drops from operational heights. Unlike commercial ultrabooks, they retain native RS232 serial ports and RJ45 Gigabit Ethernet jacks, enabling direct, adapter-free connections to factory scan tools, Pass-Thru interfaces, and shop-floor networks.

A standout feature for continuous operations is the dual hot-swappable battery architecture. Technicians can replace a depleted pack without shutting down the system or interrupting an in-progress flash or full-vehicle scan. The touch displays are further optimized for gloved and wet-hand operation, a practical necessity when working beneath lifts or in outdoor rescue scenarios. Together, these characteristics form the underlying reliability fabric that allows an AI-ready rugged laptop or AI-powered industrial tablet to run diagnostic software and execute diagnostic tasks without compromise, even in environments where consumer hardware would have long since failed.

On-Device AI: From Reading Codes to Running Inference

As Automotive Diagnostics moves from simple fault-code retrieval to pattern recognition across live data streams, guided fault isolation, and predictive health checks, cloud-dependent AI becomes a liability. Repair bays, underground garages, and roadside assistance locations rarely offer stable high-bandwidth connectivity. Meanwhile, regulatory and customer demands for data sovereignty require that sensitive vehicle diagnostic information remain local.

Emdoor Info's answer is to place inference capability directly in the technician's hands. Its rugged AI PC portfolio integrates neural processing units (NPUs) within a heterogeneous CPU-plus-GPU-plus-NPU architecture. For example, the EM-A15, powered by an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 processor, delivers up to 126 tera operations per second (TOPS) of total heterogeneous compute—enough to run medium-parameter diagnostic assistance models and analyze multiple ECU data streams in parallel. For all-day field operations requiring balanced power efficiency, the EM-X14M and EM-I14M utilize Intel Core Ultra processors, leveraging a tri-core heterogeneous design to sustain continuous AI inference without exhausting battery reserves.

This architecture transforms the rugged AI PC from a passive display into an intelligent edge node capable of pre-diagnosis planning, real-time anomaly detection, and guided troubleshooting entirely offline.

Emdoor Info segments the diagnostic workflow into three AI-enhanced stages, each executed locally on the device.

First, Intelligent Planning. Before a vehicle enters the service bay, the terminal establishes a secure connection via Gigabit Ethernet or WLAN, reads ECU topology, historical diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), and freeze-frame data, and runs a local planning engine. The system generates a standardized diagnostic path, matches the required specialty tools, and estimates labor time—compressing idle bay time and replacing experiential guesswork with a data-driven starting point.

Second, AI-Based Diagnostics. Modern intelligent vehicles generate massive data flows from 60 to 100 ECUs. Emdoor Info's terminals aggregate encrypted multi-ECU streams and run computer-vision models and anomaly-detection agents at the edge. On high-NPU models such as the EM-A14, EM-A15, EM-I10L, and EM-I20L, this analysis occurs in real time at the workstation, eliminating the round-trip latency and bandwidth constraints of cloud processing while ensuring that Raw ECU streams and sensitive diagnostic data never leaves the device.

Third, Digital Technical Support. After retrieving a fault code, technicians often face the harder question: what to check next. Here, an AI-ready rugged laptop or AI-powered industrial tablet running a lightweight large language model (LLM) combined with a structured repair knowledge base and vehicle-specific case libraries translates codes and observed symptoms into step-by-step troubleshooting guidance. When network access is available, the processed outputs—diagnostic results, repair reports, and full service records—sync automatically to backend management systems, creating a closed-loop maintenance history.

Choosing the Right Device for the Diagnostic Load

For systems integrators, distributors, and fleet operators, selecting the right device, whether a rugged AI tablet or a rugged AI laptop, is critical to matching compute level to workload. Emdoor Info's portfolio spans 33 to 126 TOPS to address specific diagnostic intensities.

Beyond Automotive: Extending into More Scenarios

While Automotive Diagnostics is a primary use case, the same on-device NPU compute, industrial interface set, and MIL-STD-810H ruggedization extend into adjacent verticals. Industrial vision inspection teams use the platform for real-time defect recognition on production lines. Security operators deploy it for edge video analytics in the field. Unmanned aerial system command units rely on its local mission planning and video-stream processing capabilities. For channel partners and distributors, this versatility means a single rugged AI PC platform can address multiple market segments without duplicating engineering or logistics efforts. Emdoor's global manufacturing footprint and long product-lifecycle support further reduce total cost of ownership for enterprise deployments at scale.

The modern vehicle is a software-defined system, and servicing it demands tools that are equally intelligent, connected, and indestructible. data.title: Solo Brings Human Verification to Venmo Co-Founder's JellyJelly App as AI Agents Beat CAPTCHA
data.description:
Image: Solo

Solo's SDK confirms that each JellyJelly account belongs to a real, unique person, after a Solo AI agent passed CAPTCHA on 50+ Discord servers.

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Solo, a privacy-preserving proof-of-humanity company, is bringing its human verification software development kit (SDK) to JellyJelly. The social video app runs on Solana and was co-founded by Venmo co-founder Iqram Magdon-Ismail. The integration lets JellyJelly confirm that every account belongs to a real, unique person, with no government ID and no puzzles to solve.

Magdon-Ismail is co-founder and CEO of JellyJelly and an advisor to Solo. He co-developed the SDK behind the integration, shaping both its architecture and the way new users are onboarded.

The move comes as AI agents learn to pass the tests meant to keep them out. In an experiment run by Solo, an AI agent named Gary joined more than 50 Discord servers overnight and sent over 500 messages. No one identified it as an AI agent.

Gary had two instructions: pass every CAPTCHA challenge and accept the terms of service. It completed both through ordinary browsing and clicking, without any custom exploits.

Solo reads the result as a weakness in CAPTCHA. The challenges test whether a visitor can solve a puzzle, and capable AI agents can solve the same puzzles. Harder tests add friction for legitimate users, but they do little to show that a human is behind an account.

"CAPTCHA was built around the idea that humans could do things bots couldn't. That's becoming a harder assumption to make when AI agents can browse, click and solve the same challenges as people," said Edison Siu, co-founder and CEO of Solo. "Our approach is to verify the human directly. Platforms need to know they're dealing with a real person. Users shouldn't have to struggle through more puzzles or upload identity documents to prove it."

JellyJelly lets users share short videos and send cryptocurrency payments to one another. The rise of AI-generated video and automated accounts has made it harder for social platforms to know who is behind each account. Solo's SDK brings human verification into that setting. It helps the platform tell genuine users from automated accounts, and it stops one person from registering several verified identities.

The process starts with a facial scan from a standard smartphone camera. Solo converts the scan into a biometric representation and encrypts it on the device using fully homomorphic encryption (FHE). This type of encryption lets a system work on data without ever decrypting it. Solo uses it to compare the encrypted representation against existing records, so the matching step never exposes the underlying data.

Users do not need special hardware or a government-issued ID. Raw facial images are not stored. Apps that use the SDK receive a verification result, not access to anyone's biometric information.

The same SDK can be added to gaming platforms, payment services and other applications that need to block duplicate accounts or separate real users from automated activity.

Solo is backed by Draper Associates, the venture firm founded by Tim Draper. Draper Associates led a $1 million round in the company in March 2025. Solo was also selected for cohort 5 of the Solana Incubator.

Solo's human verification technology is already live. The company is now working on tools that would let verified users authorize their own AI agents, so merchants and online platforms can confirm that a real, unique person stands behind each one. Solo also plans to enable AI agents and AI companies to pay verified people for work that only humans can do.

Magdon-Ismail, who co-founded Venmo and helped develop its peer-to-peer payment system, is advising Solo on how people and their AI agents will pay and get paid.

"Venmo made it easy to pay a friend," said Magdon-Ismail. "The next step is your AI agent paying on your behalf. The business receiving that payment needs to know a real person authorized it. I'm working with Solo to make that process simple for everyone involved."

About Solo

Solo develops proof-of-humanity technology that lets online platforms check that a user is a real, unique person, without asking who that person is. Its smartphone-based system uses fully homomorphic encryption to compare encrypted biometric data, and partners receive a verification result instead of raw biometric data. Solo provides an SDK for web and mobile applications. The company is backed by Draper Associates and was selected for the Solana Incubator cohort 5. Its first product, SoloMission, lets AI agents collect feedback from verified humans.

data.title: US STOCKS-Wall St reverses early gains as Nvidia fallout rattles tech stocks
data.description:
* Indexes down: Dow 0.41%, S&P 500 0.93%, Nasdaq 1.42%

* Microsoft ( MSFT ) down after global outage

* Nvidia ( NVDA ) falls further following Jensen Huang's exit

(Updates after market open)

By Niket Nishant and Utkarsh Hathi

Nov 13 (Reuters) - The major US stock indexes fell on Friday as investors weighed the potential ripple effects of Jensen Huang's exit as Nvidia ( NVDA ) chief executive, while softer October producer prices offered little relief.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares slipped 3.3% and were on track for their longest streak of weekly losses since October 2012 after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, following scrutiny of his relationship with a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for Chinese intelligence.

The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 5%, with Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) dropping 9.4% and 5.8%, respectively.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius ( NBIS ) shed 10% and 13.7%, respectively, while data center-related firms IREN ( IREN ) , Applied Digital ( APLD ) and Core Scientific ( CORZ ) traded sharply lower.

The turmoil at Nvidia ( NVDA ) has raised concerns about the broader AI trade, given the chipmaker's central role in the industry's boom and its financial ties to several companies in the sector.

Anthropic's much-anticipated initial public offering next week is also on the radar.

"Something that will be interesting to see is if all the supply of new equity is going to be absorbed in a way that doesn't result in selling other AI stocks to kind of fund that," said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global investment strategist at Edward Jones.

Among the Magnificent Seven, Apple ( AAPL ) and Meta were the only gainers, rising more than 1% each. Microsoft ( MSFT ) was down 0.6% after a more than 12-hour outage of Outlook and Teams.

At 10:16 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 215.69 points, or 0.41%, to 52,081.40, the S&P 500 lost 70.60 points, or 0.93%, to 7,519.10 and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 359.89 points, or 1.42%, to 25,006.20.

Losses in the tech sector index weighed on the S&P 500.

Data showed October producer prices were slightly softer than expected, potentially relieving some pressure on the US Federal Reserve to hike interest rates aggressively.

Traders are fully pricing in a hike by the central bank next month, with some policymakers in recent days raising the prospect of a 50-basis-point increase, compared to a widely expected 25 bps rise. Odds of a 50-bps hike sit around 7%, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"I think they're going to move more gradually. Inflation is elevated and at uncomfortable levels for the Fed, but there's no sign that it is getting out of hand," Kourkafas said.

In other movers, Cerebras jumped more than 11% after the chip and cloud company raised its 2026 revenue forecast and signed Microsoft ( MSFT ) as a customer.

Strong earnings have at certain points kept the negative market sentiment in check this week. Of the 450 companies in the S&P 500 that reported earnings as of Thursday, 83.6% surpassed expectations, according to Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings and equity research at LSEG Data and Analytics.

Still, investors are wary of a bunch of risks, including on the geopolitical front. Oil prices were in positive territory for the third consecutive session, a day after President Donald Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.53-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 2.07-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 7 new 52-week highs and 1 new low, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 16 new highs and 195 new lows.

(Reporting by Niket Nishant and Utkarsh Hathi in Bengaluru; Editing by Shinjini Ganguli and Pooja Desai)
